about: A typed map of mathematical transformations: input, output, preserved and broken invariants, functional tags. Landed entries, an authored fill layer, and receipted additions; every entry states its origin.

terms.name: Birational type
terms.definition: The class of a variety up to birational equivalence: isomorphism of dense open subsets.

terms.name: Function field
terms.definition: The field of rational functions of an irreducible variety, as an extension of the base field.

terms.name: Local structure at the center
terms.definition: The germ of the space along the locus a surgery is performed on.

terms.name: Presence of the exceptional divisor
terms.definition: Whether the divisor created by a blow-up is present as a curve (or divisor) in the space.

terms.name: Self-intersection number
terms.definition: The intersection number of a curve with itself on a surface, C^2.

terms.name: Isomorphism type of a curve
terms.definition: The curve up to isomorphism, as an abstract curve.

terms.name: Homotopy type
terms.definition: The space up to homotopy equivalence.

terms.name: Contractibility
terms.definition: Being homotopy equivalent to a point.

terms.name: Topology of the input
terms.definition: The input space's topology as given, before any collapse or gluing.

terms.name: Point positions and distances
terms.definition: The positions of the input points and the distances between them.

terms.name: Limits
terms.definition: Limits of diagrams (all small limits, where stated), preserved when a functor carries limit cones to limit cones.

terms.name: Finite limits
terms.definition: Limits of finite diagrams: the terminal object, pullbacks, equalizers.

terms.name: Colimits
terms.definition: Colimits of diagrams, preserved when a functor carries colimit cocones to colimit cocones.

terms.name: Category structure
terms.definition: The objects and morphisms of a category with their composition.

terms.name: Truth values
terms.definition: The subobject classifier's elements: the internal truth values of a topos.

terms.name: Skeletal objects of a level
terms.definition: The objects fixed by a level's skeleton modality (i-skeleta).

terms.name: Opposition at a level
terms.definition: The distinction, at one level, between its skeleta and its sheaves.

terms.name: L^2 orthogonality
terms.definition: Pieces of a decomposition are mutually orthogonal in the L^2 inner product.

terms.name: Cohomology
terms.definition: De Rham or singular cohomology groups.

terms.name: The function itself (by resummation)
terms.definition: The decomposed pieces sum back to the original function.

terms.name: Spatial locality
terms.definition: Support or concentration in physical space.

terms.name: Instantaneous locality
terms.definition: An effect at time t depends only on the source at time t.

terms.name: Linearity
terms.definition: Superposition: the response to a sum is the sum of the responses.

terms.name: Causality
terms.definition: Only earlier times contribute to the state at a given time.

terms.name: Leibniz rule
terms.definition: The product rule for derivations.

terms.name: Tensoriality
terms.definition: Linearity over smooth functions (C-infinity linearity) in an argument.

terms.name: Flatness
terms.definition: Vanishing curvature: covariant derivatives commute.

origins.clone:<id>: a pointer resolved to its home entry
origins.added: an entry the map lacked, each claim receipted by a verbatim quote (receipts)

entries.name: Transpose graph
entries.description: Reverses all edge orientations in a directed graph. Each directed edge (u,v) becomes (v,u).
entries.output: Directed graph G^T = (V, E') where E' = {(v,u) : (u,v) in E}
entries.preserved: Vertex set, strongly connected components (as sets), degree sequence (in/out swapped)
entries.broken: Edge orientation, directed path structure, reachability ordering

entries.name: Complement graph
entries.description: Produces the graph on the same vertex set where two vertices are adjacent if and only if they are not adjacent in the original.
entries.broken: All adjacencies inverted, edge count (complemented to n(n-1)/2 - |E|), clique/independent set duality
entries.complexity: O(|V|^2) to construct adjacency; O(1) conceptually

entries.name: Line graph
entries.description: Constructs a new graph L(G) whose vertices are the edges of G, with two vertices in L(G) adjacent when their corresponding edges in G share an incident vertex. Translates Eulerian cycles to Hamiltonian cycles. Iterated application yields deterministic terminal behaviors (stabilizes as cycle, collapses, terminates as triangle, or expands). Whitney Isomorphism Theorem: G is recoverable from L(G) for connected graphs except K_3 vs K_{1,3}.
entries.output: Undirected graph L(G) = (E, E') where E' encodes edge-adjacency
entries.preserved: Edge count becomes vertex count; Eulerian property translates to Hamiltonian property
entries.broken: Vertex-edge distinction (edges become vertices), vertex count, degree distribution

formal.note: The line graph is a simple graph on G.edgeSet: its vertices are the edges of G, so edge count becomes vertex count by definition.
Two edges are adjacent in L(G) iff they are distinct and share a vertex. The entry's further claims (Eulerian to Hamiltonian, Whitney's theorem) are not in Mathlib at the pin.

entries.name: Graph minor
entries.description: A graph H obtained from G by any sequence of edge deletions, vertex deletions, and edge contractions. The Graph Minor Theorem (Robertson-Seymour) establishes that the minor ordering is a well-quasi-ordering, enabling forbidden minor characterizations of graph families.
entries.input: Graph G + specification of deletion/contraction operations
entries.preserved: Topological properties characterized by forbidden minors (planarity, bounded treewidth, linkless embeddability)
entries.broken: Vertex/edge count, specific structure, metric properties
entries.complexity: Polynomial per operation; minor testing is NP-complete in general

entries.name: Graph rewriting
entries.description: Replaces a subgraph matching a specified pattern with a different subgraph according to a production rule. General framework encompassing many local graph transformations.
entries.input: Graph G + rewrite rule (pattern subgraph, replacement subgraph, embedding specification)
entries.complexity: Depends on rewrite rule; subgraph matching is NP-complete in general

entries.name: Power of graph (G^k)
entries.description: Connects vertices whose path distance in G is at most k. For a graph of diameter d, G^d is complete. Monotone in connectivity. G^2 models wireless interference (vertices sharing common neighbors). Determining whether a graph is the square of another is NP-complete.
entries.input: Graph G = (V, E) + positive integer k
entries.output: Dense graph G^k = (V, E') where (u,v) in E' iff dist_G(u,v) <= k
entries.broken: Sparsity, path structure, distance metric (collapsed), chromatic number (may increase)
entries.complexity: O(|V|^3) via matrix multiplication (BFS per vertex: O(|V|(|V|+|E|)))

entries.name: Dual graph
entries.description: For a plane graph, constructs a new graph with a vertex for each face of the original and an edge for each pair of faces sharing a boundary edge. Captures planar topology.
entries.broken: Vertex-face distinction (vertices become faces and vice versa), degree distribution

entries.name: Medial graph
entries.description: Constructs a 4-regular graph from a planar graph by placing a vertex on each edge and connecting consecutive edge-vertices around each face.
entries.preserved: Planarity, edge count encoded as vertex count
entries.broken: Degree distribution (forced to 4-regular), original vertex/face structure

entries.name: Quotient graph
entries.description: Collapses each block of a vertex partition into a single super-vertex. Edges between blocks in the original produce edges between super-vertices.
entries.input: Graph G = (V, E) + partition P of V
entries.output: Quotient graph G/P with vertices = blocks of P
entries.broken: Individual vertex identity, internal block structure, vertex count

entries.name: Double graph
entries.description: Creates a graph containing two copies of G with additional edges connecting corresponding vertices and their neighborhoods across copies.

entries.name: Simplex graph
entries.description: Constructs a graph whose vertices represent the cliques of G (including the empty set), with edges between cliques differing by exactly one vertex.
entries.output: Simplex graph S(G) (clique complex encoded as graph)
entries.preserved: Clique structure of G encoded in vertex set of S(G)
entries.broken: Original vertex/edge structure, graph size (exponential blowup possible)
entries.complexity: Exponential in general (output size exponential in clique number)

entries.name: YΔ-transformation (Wye-Delta)
entries.description: Replaces a star subgraph (Y-configuration, K_{1,3}) with a triangle subgraph (Δ-configuration, K_3), preserving electrical resistance and network flow properties. The internal central node is eliminated; the three peripheral nodes become mutually adjacent.
entries.input: Graph G containing a degree-3 vertex v with neighbors {a,b,c}
entries.output: Graph G' with v removed and edges {ab, bc, ac} added (with appropriate resistance weights)
entries.preserved: Electrical resistance between external terminals, network flow properties, external terminal behavior
entries.broken: Internal node structure, vertex count (reduced by 1), edge count (may change), planarity (may be broken)

entries.name: ΔY-transformation (Delta-Wye)
entries.description: Inverse of YΔ. Replaces a triangle subgraph (Δ-configuration) with a star subgraph (Y-configuration), introducing a new internal node.
entries.input: Graph G containing a triangle on vertices {a,b,c}
entries.output: Graph G' with edges {ab, bc, ac} removed and new vertex v added with edges {va, vb, vc}
entries.preserved: Electrical resistance between external terminals, network flow properties
entries.broken: Internal node structure, vertex count (increased by 1)

entries.name: Mycielskian
entries.description: Constructs a larger graph M(G) that preserves triangle-freeness while strictly increasing the chromatic number. Provides the constructive proof that triangle-free graphs can have arbitrarily high chromatic number.
entries.output: Triangle-free graph M(G) with |V(M(G))| = 2|V| + 1, χ(M(G)) = χ(G) + 1
entries.broken: Chromatic number (strictly increased by 1), vertex count (more than doubled), edge count

entries.name: Graph union
entries.description: Binary operation producing a graph whose vertex set and edge set are the unions of the two input graphs' vertex and edge sets.
entries.preserved: All structure from both inputs preserved (subgraph containment)
entries.broken: Connectivity (may increase or decrease), component structure

entries.name: Graph intersection
entries.description: Binary operation producing a graph containing only vertices and edges common to both inputs.
entries.input: Graphs G_1 = (V_1, E_1), G_2 = (V_2, E_2) with V_1 = V_2

entries.name: Graph join
entries.description: Takes the union of two graphs and adds all possible edges between vertices of the two graphs.
entries.input: Graphs G_1, G_2 (typically on disjoint vertex sets)
entries.output: Graph G_1 + G_2 with complete bipartite edges between V_1 and V_2
entries.preserved: Internal structure of each input graph
entries.broken: Independence between the two graphs (fully connected), sparsity

entries.name: Cartesian graph product
entries.description: Binary operation producing a graph on vertex set V_1 x V_2 where (u_1,u_2) and (v_1,v_2) are adjacent iff u_1=v_1 and u_2~v_2, or u_2=v_2 and u_1~v_1. Creates grid-like expansions. Commutative and associative for unlabelled graphs.
entries.output: Graph G_1 □ G_2 on V_1 x V_2
entries.preserved: Commutativity, associativity; each factor graph embedded as induced subgraph

entries.name: Rooted graph product
entries.description: Associative composition for unlabelled rooted structures. Merges rooted graphs at designated root vertices.

entries.name: Tensor graph product
entries.description: Binary operation where (u_1,u_2) and (v_1,v_2) are adjacent iff u_1~v_1 AND u_2~v_2. Adjacencies require simultaneous adjacency in both factors. The categorical product in the category of graphs.
entries.output: Graph G_1 ⊗ G_2 on V_1 x V_2
entries.broken: Connectivity (often sparser than factors), vertex count (multiplied)

entries.name: Series-parallel graph composition
entries.description: Constructs networks by sequential (series) concatenation of two-terminal graphs. The resulting class is efficiently analyzable for flow, resistance, and connectivity.
entries.input: Two-terminal graphs (G_1, s_1, t_1), (G_2, s_2, t_2)
entries.output: Two-terminal graph with t_1 identified with s_2

entries.name: Parallel graph composition
entries.description: Constructs networks by identifying the source terminals and sink terminals of two two-terminal graphs. Commutative.
entries.input: Two-terminal graphs (G_1, s_1, t_1), (G_2, s_2, t_2)
entries.output: Two-terminal graph with s_1=s_2 and t_1=t_2

entries.name: Hajós construction
entries.description: Binary operation: removes one edge from each of two graphs, identifies a vertex from each removed edge, and connects the remaining endpoints. All graphs of chromatic number k can be generated by iterated Hajós construction from complete graph K_k.
entries.input: Graphs G_1, G_2 each with a designated edge
entries.preserved: Chromatic number lower bound (monotonically builds toward target χ)

entries.name: Induced subgraph
entries.description: Selects a vertex subset S and retains all edges of G between vertices in S. The subgraph is fully determined by the vertex subset.
entries.input: Graph G = (V, E) + vertex subset S ⊆ V
entries.output: Induced subgraph G[S] = (S, E ∩ (S x S))
entries.preserved: All adjacencies within the selected subset, induced subgraph hereditary properties
entries.broken: Vertices outside S, edges incident to deleted vertices

entries.name: Block graph
entries.description: Constructs a graph whose vertices represent the biconnected components (blocks) of G, with edges between blocks sharing a cut vertex.

entries.name: Block-cut graph
entries.description: Bipartite graph with one vertex class for blocks and one for cut vertices, with edges indicating containment. Always a tree (or forest).

entries.name: Deck
entries.description: The multiset of all vertex-deleted subgraphs of G. Each card in the deck is G with one vertex (and its incident edges) removed. Central to the graph reconstruction conjecture.
entries.output: Multiset of n graphs, each on n-1 vertices
entries.preserved: Encodes (conjecturally) all structural information of G for n >= 3
entries.broken: Individual vertex identity (each card loses a different vertex)

entries.name: Reconstruction
entries.description: The (conjectured) inverse of the deck operation: recovering G from its deck of vertex-deleted subgraphs. The reconstruction conjecture asserts this is possible for all graphs on 3+ vertices.
entries.complexity: Open problem in general; polynomial for specific graph classes

entries.name: Root
entries.description: Designates a distinguished vertex in a graph or tree, converting an unrooted structure into a rooted one. Induces parent-child relationships and level structure.
entries.output: Rooted graph/tree (G, r) with induced hierarchy
entries.preserved: Underlying graph structure, vertex set, edge set
entries.broken: Vertex symmetry (root is distinguished), undirected traversal equivalence

entries.name: Transitive closure
entries.description: For a directed graph, adds edge (u,v) whenever there exists a directed path from u to v. The result encodes reachability as direct adjacency.
entries.output: Directed graph G+ = (V, E+) where (u,v) in E+ iff u can reach v in G
entries.broken: Sparsity (potentially dense), path structure (collapsed to direct edges)

entries.name: Transitive reduction
entries.description: Removes edges that are implied by transitivity, producing the sparsest graph with the same reachability relation. Unique for DAGs.
entries.output: Directed graph G- = (V, E-) with same reachability, minimal edge set
entries.complexity: O(|V| * |E|) in general; O(|V| + |E|) for DAGs

entries.name: k-tree
entries.description: Recursive construction: start with K_{k+1}, iteratively add vertices each adjacent to exactly k mutually adjacent existing vertices. k-trees are the maximal graphs of treewidth k.
entries.broken: N/A (constructive, not a transformation of an existing graph)
entries.complexity: O(n) per vertex addition (n = number of vertices)

entries.name: Tree decomposition
entries.description: Maps a graph G into a tree T whose nodes carry vertex subsets ("bags") of G. Every edge of G lies in some bag; bags containing any given vertex form a connected subtree. Minimizing maximum bag size minus one yields the treewidth. Translates cyclic dependencies into acyclic framework.
entries.output: Tree T with bag function β: V(T) -> 2^V satisfying running intersection
entries.complexity: NP-complete to minimize width; O(2^O(tw) * n) to compute given width tw

entries.name: Branch-decomposition
entries.description: Alternative hierarchical clustering of edges represented by an unrooted binary tree with leaves bijectively mapped to edges. Minimizing the maximum order of separations yields branchwidth.
entries.output: Unrooted binary tree with leaves = E, separations at internal edges
entries.complexity: NP-complete to minimize width in general; polynomial for planar graphs

entries.name: Path decomposition
entries.description: Strict restriction of tree decomposition where the tree is a path. Optimizes pathwidth (vertex separation number). Used in VLSI design and register allocation.
entries.output: Path P with bag function β satisfying running intersection

entries.name: Symmetric difference
entries.description: Binary operation on graphs with the same vertex set: the resulting edge set contains edges present in exactly one of the two inputs.
entries.input: Graphs G_1 = (V, E_1), G_2 = (V, E_2) on the same vertex set
entries.broken: Shared edges removed, unique edges retained

entries.name: Disjoint union
entries.description: Union of graphs on disjoint vertex sets. Produces a disconnected graph with one component per input.
entries.input: Graphs G_1, G_2 (vertex sets relabelled to be disjoint)
entries.preserved: Each input graph fully preserved as a component
entries.broken: Connectivity (guaranteed disconnected if both inputs nonempty)

entries.name: Book embedding
entries.description: Maps vertices to a line (spine) and assigns edges to half-planes (pages) such that edges on the same page do not cross. Minimizing pages yields the book thickness.
entries.output: Linear ordering of V + page assignment for E
entries.broken: Vertex symmetry (linear ordering imposed), edge planarity per page

entries.name: Transitive orientation
entries.description: Orients the edges of an undirected graph such that the resulting directed graph has the transitivity property: if a->b and b->c then a->c. Possible exactly for comparability graphs.
entries.complexity: O(|V| + |E|) for comparability graphs via modular decomposition

entries.name: Chordal completion (triangulation)
entries.description: Adds edges to eliminate all induced cycles of length >= 4, making the graph chordal. Directly equivalent to Gaussian elimination fill-in of sparse symmetric matrices: minimal chordal completion corresponds to a fill-in pattern, and the elimination ordering derives from the resulting chordal graph. Minimum chordal completion and minimum fill-in are both NP-complete.
entries.output: Chordal graph G' = (V, E ∪ F) where F is the fill edge set
entries.preserved: Vertex set, original edges (augmentation only), connectivity
entries.broken: Sparsity (edges added), induced cycle structure (all long cycles get chords)
entries.complexity: NP-complete (minimum fill-in); polynomial for minimal completion

entries.name: Minimal chordal completion
entries.description: A chordal completion where no proper subset of the added fill edges also yields a chordal graph. Not necessarily minimum (fewest edges).
entries.output: Chordal graph G' with inclusion-minimal fill set
entries.preserved: Same as D1-040, plus minimality of fill under inclusion
entries.broken: Sparsity (edges added), induced cycle structure (all long cycles get chords)
entries.complexity: Polynomial (e.g., LEX-BFS ordering yields minimal completion in O(n*m))

entries.name: Minimum chordal completion
entries.description: A chordal completion using the fewest possible fill edges. NP-complete to compute. Corresponds to the minimum fill-in problem in numerical linear algebra.
entries.output: Chordal graph G' with cardinality-minimal fill set
entries.preserved: Same as D1-040, plus optimality of fill count
entries.broken: Sparsity (edges added), induced cycle structure (all long cycles get chords)

entries.name: Maximum clique minimization
entries.description: Seeks a chordal completion that minimizes the size of the largest clique in the resulting chordal graph. Equivalent to minimizing treewidth.

entries.name: Interval completion
entries.description: Adds edges to make the graph an interval graph. Characterizes graph families like AT-free graphs via their completion properties.

entries.name: Proper interval completion
entries.description: Adds edges to produce a proper interval graph, bounding the bandwidth of the network. Stricter than interval completion.

entries.name: Edge deletion
entries.description: Removes a specified edge from the graph, preserving all vertices. Elementary graph surgery.
entries.input: Graph G = (V, E) + edge e in E
entries.preserved: Vertex set, all other edges, vertex degrees (except endpoints of e, reduced by 1)

entries.name: Vertex deletion
entries.description: Removes a specified vertex and all its incident edges.
entries.input: Graph G = (V, E) + vertex v in V
entries.output: Graph G - v = (V \ {v}, E restricted to V \ {v})
entries.preserved: Induced subgraph structure on remaining vertices
entries.broken: Vertex count (reduced by 1), all edges incident to v removed, connectivity (may disconnect)

entries.name: Edge contraction
entries.description: Removes an edge and merges its two endpoints into a single vertex, inheriting all adjacencies of both. Fundamental operation in graph minor theory.
entries.input: Graph G = (V, E) + edge e = {u,v} in E
entries.output: Graph G/e with u,v merged into single vertex w
entries.preserved: Topological properties closed under minors (planarity, bounded treewidth, etc.)
entries.broken: Vertex count (reduced by 1), simplicity (may create parallel edges), specific adjacency pattern

entries.name: Graph coarsening
entries.description: Reduces vertex set by aggregating nodes into super-nodes, preserving global structural properties. Used in multi-level partition algorithms.
entries.output: Coarser graph G' with fewer vertices
entries.broken: Individual vertex identity, fine-grained structure, vertex count

entries.name: Graph condensation
entries.description: Contracts each strongly connected component of a directed graph into a single super-vertex. The result is always a DAG.
entries.preserved: Reachability between components, DAG structure of component relationships
entries.broken: Internal SCC structure, individual vertex identity within components

entries.name: Graph sparsification
entries.description: Reduces edge count while approximately preserving spectral, cut, or distance properties. Spectral sparsifiers approximate the Laplacian quadratic form; cut sparsifiers approximate all cut values.
entries.input: Graph G = (V, E) + approximation parameter ε
entries.output: Sparse graph G' = (V, E') with |E'| << |E| and property approximation within (1±ε)
entries.preserved: Spectral properties (approximately), cut values (approximately), vertex set
entries.broken: Exact edge structure, edge count (drastically reduced)
entries.complexity: O(|E| log^c |V| / epsilon^2) for spectral sparsifiers

entries.name: Kron reduction
entries.description: Eliminates a subset of interior nodes from a graph while preserving effective resistance distances between remaining boundary nodes. Algebraically equivalent to computing the Schur complement of the graph Laplacian. Provides robust spectral interlacing guarantees superior to heuristic contraction methods.
entries.input: Graph G with Laplacian L, partition of V into boundary B and interior I
entries.output: Reduced graph on B with Laplacian L/L_{II} (Schur complement)
entries.preserved: Effective resistance between boundary nodes, spectral interlacing of Laplacian, network sparsity (approximately)
entries.broken: Interior node structure, vertex count (reduced to |B|), specific edge weights
entries.complexity: O(|I|^3) for Schur complement computation (|I| = interior node count)

entries.name: Greedy iterative contraction
entries.description: Heuristic graph reduction that iteratively contracts edges selected by a greedy criterion (e.g., heaviest edge, minimum degree). Lacks the spectral guarantees of Kron reduction.

entries.name: Heavy-edge matching
entries.description: Selects a maximal matching prioritizing edges with largest weights, then contracts matched pairs. Standard coarsening phase in multi-level partitioning (e.g., METIS).
entries.output: Coarsened graph with matched vertex pairs merged
entries.preserved: Approximate partition quality, total edge weight (approximately)
entries.broken: Individual vertex identity, vertex count (halved approximately)

entries.name: Data augmentation on graphs
entries.description: Generates perturbed copies of a graph (edge dropout, node dropout, subgraph sampling, feature masking) for graph neural network training.

entries.name: Graph surgery
entries.description: General term for local structural modifications to a graph (cutting and reattaching edges, replacing subgraphs). Umbrella term covering many specific operations.

entries.name: Matroid deletion (restriction)
entries.description: Removes an element from the ground set. Independent sets of the result are exactly the independent sets of the original that do not contain the deleted element. In matrix representation, corresponds to column removal.
entries.input: Matroid M = (E, I) + element e in E
entries.preserved: Independence of all sets not involving e, rank function restricted to subsets of E \ {e}
entries.broken: Ground set size (reduced by 1), circuits/bases involving e
entries.complexity: O(1) for independence oracle model; O(n) for matrix representation

entries.name: Matroid contraction
entries.description: Contracts an element: the resulting matroid has ground set E \ {e} with rank function r'(A) = r(A ∪ {e}) - r({e}). In matrix representation, corresponds to projecting remaining vectors onto quotient space. Dual to matroid deletion in M*.
entries.input: Matroid M = (E, I) + element e in E
entries.broken: Ground set size, rank (reduced if e was not a loop), absolute independence
entries.complexity: O(r * n) for matrix representation (r = rank)

entries.name: Matroid dual
entries.description: Constructs M* on the same ground set where bases of M* are set-theoretic complements of bases of M. Contraction in M = deletion in M*, and vice versa. For graphic matroids of planar graphs, the dual matroid equals the cycle matroid of the dual graph.
entries.output: Matroid M* = (E, B*) where B* = {E \ B : B in B}
entries.preserved: Ground set, matroid axioms, representability over same field (when applicable)
entries.broken: Basis structure (complemented), rank (r* = |E| - r), independence structure
entries.complexity: Exponential in general (basis enumeration); O(1) conceptual

formal.note: Bases of the dual are the complements, within the ground set, of bases of M.
The dual has the same ground set.
r + r* = |E|, the entry's rank formula, stated in extended naturals so it covers infinite ground sets.

entries.name: Matroid minor
entries.description: Result of any sequence of deletion and contraction operations. Gives rise to forbidden minor characterizations of matroid classes. Well-quasi-ordering under the minor relation (for matroids representable over finite fields).
entries.input: Matroid M + sequence of deletion/contraction operations
entries.preserved: Properties closed under minors (representability over given field, excluded minor characterizations)
entries.broken: Ground set size, rank, specific structure
entries.complexity: Polynomial per operation; minor containment testing is NP-complete

entries.name: Matroid direct sum
entries.description: Combines two matroids on disjoint ground sets. Independent sets of the sum are unions of independent sets from each component. Mirrors disjoint graph union.
entries.input: Matroids M_1 = (E_1, I_1), M_2 = (E_2, I_2) with E_1 ∩ E_2 = ∅
entries.preserved: Independence structure of each component, rank is additive
entries.broken: Connectedness (result is disconnected if both inputs nonempty)

entries.name: Matroid 2-sum (Seymour)
entries.description: Specialized amalgamation gluing two matroids along a common element. Used in structural decomposition of connected matroids.
entries.input: Matroids M_1, M_2 sharing a single common element p
entries.broken: The shared element p is typically removed from the ground set

entries.name: Matroid 3-sum (Seymour)
entries.description: Glues two binary matroids across a common triangle (3-element set), then deletes those elements. Analogous to gluing graphs across a triangle. Foundational in structural decomposition of 3-connected binary matroids.
entries.input: Binary matroids M_1, M_2 sharing a 3-element circuit-hyperplane
entries.complexity: Polynomial in ground set size (binary matroids only)

entries.name: Matroid union
entries.description: Given matroids M_1, ..., M_k on the same ground set, the union matroid has as independent sets those expressible as unions of independent sets from each M_i. Mirrors spanning forest synthesis in graphs.
entries.input: Matroids M_1, ..., M_k on common ground set E

entries.name: Matroid relaxation
entries.description: Converts a circuit-hyperplane (a set that is both a circuit and a hyperplane) into an independent basis. Strictly increases the number of bases. Can map representable matroids into non-representable territory. Used to identify excluded minors for field representability.
entries.output: Relaxed matroid M' with B' = B ∪ {C}
entries.preserved: Ground set, all bases except the new one
entries.broken: Circuit structure (C is no longer a circuit), representability (may be lost)

entries.name: Matroid truncation
entries.description: Uniformly restricts the rank of a matroid by 1 (or more). Independent sets of the truncation are those independent sets of rank at most r-1. Flattens the geometric hierarchy.
entries.output: Truncated matroid T(M) of rank r-1
entries.preserved: Ground set, independence of sets of rank < r
entries.broken: Rank (reduced), bases (all former bases become dependent)

entries.name: Transversal presentation
entries.description: Represents a matroid via a bipartite graph where independent sets correspond to sets with a system of distinct representatives (a matching covering the set).
entries.output: Bipartite graph encoding the matroid's independence structure

entries.name: Valuated matroid transformation
entries.description: Extends classical matroid theory by assigning a valuation (weight function) to the bases satisfying a tropical exchange axiom. Connects matroid theory to tropical geometry.
entries.input: Matroid M + valuation function w: B -> R satisfying tropical Plücker relations
entries.preserved: Underlying matroid structure, tropical exchange axiom
entries.broken: Unweighted matroid symmetry (bases now have distinct valuations)

entries.name: Perfect matroid design transformation
entries.description: Constructs matroids where all flats of any given rank have equal cardinality. Maps irregular matroid structures into perfectly symmetric structures of balanced incomplete block designs (BIBDs) and Steiner systems. Connects matroid theory to finite projective and affine geometries.
entries.output: Perfect matroid design (matroid with equicardinal flats per rank)
entries.preserved: Matroid axioms, flat equicardinality per rank
entries.complexity: Depends on parameters; existence is the hard problem

entries.name: Plethysm
entries.description: Operator composition f[g] treating symmetric function f as a functional operator on expressions generated by g. Nonlinear, associative. In representation theory, plethysm of Schur functions = character of composition of polynomial representations of GL_n.
entries.input: Symmetric functions f, g in Λ
entries.broken: Linearity (plethysm is nonlinear), basis decomposition complexity (outputs are large)
entries.complexity: Computationally hard; no known efficient general algorithm for Kronecker/plethysm coefficients

entries.name: Hall transformation
entries.description: Ring endomorphism mapping elementary symmetric functions to complete homogeneous: ω(e_i) = h_i. An isometric involution that mirrors conjugate transposition of integer partitions, mapping s_λ to s_{λ'}.
entries.output: Symmetric function in complete homogeneous basis (h_λ)
entries.preserved: Ring structure, algebraic independence, Schur positivity (maps Schur to Schur)
entries.complexity: O(n) where n = number of terms in the symmetric function

entries.name: Omega (ω) involution
entries.description: Same operation as D1-071 (Hall transformation). Alternative notation.
entries.output: Symmetric function in complete homogeneous basis (h_λ)
entries.preserved: Ring structure, algebraic independence, Schur positivity (maps Schur to Schur)

entries.name: Jacobi-Trudi determinant
entries.description: Determinantal formula expanding Schur functions s_λ in terms of complete homogeneous functions h. The combinatorial proof transforms algebraic permutations of matrix indices into non-intersecting lattice paths via the Lindström-Gessel-Viennot lemma.
entries.output: Schur function s_λ = det(h_{λ_i - i + j})
entries.preserved: Schur function identity, lattice path interpretation
entries.broken: Implicit basis (converts between h-basis and s-basis)
entries.complexity: O(k^3) for partition of size k (determinant computation)

entries.name: Dual Jacobi-Trudi identity
entries.description: Expands Schur functions in terms of elementary symmetric functions e instead of complete homogeneous h. Related to D1-073 by the Hall/ω involution.
entries.output: Schur function s_λ = det(e_{λ'_i - i + j}) (using conjugate partition)
entries.complexity: O(k^3) (same as D1-073 via conjugate partition)

entries.name: Robinson-Schensted-Knuth (RSK) correspondence
entries.description: Bijection mapping a two-line array (or non-negative integer matrix) to a pair of semistandard Young tableaux of the same shape (insertion tableau P, recording tableau Q). Foundational bijective proof of the Cauchy identity for Schur function products.
entries.output: Pair (P, Q) of semistandard Young tableaux with shape(P) = shape(Q)
entries.complexity: O(n^2) where n = length of input word/permutation

entries.name: Bender-Knuth involution
entries.description: Acts on adjacent alphabetic entries of a semistandard Young tableau, swapping the count of i's and (i+1)'s in each row while preserving the semistandard property. Proves the symmetry of Schur functions.
entries.input: Semistandard Young tableau T + adjacent alphabet index i
entries.output: Semistandard Young tableau T' with entries i and i+1 redistributed
entries.preserved: Shape, semistandard property, total weight (rebalanced between i and i+1)
entries.broken: Specific entry values at positions involving i and i+1
entries.complexity: O(n) where n = number of entries in tableau

entries.name: Evacuation (Schützenberger)
entries.description: Intricate involution on standard Young tableaux that reverses the order of entries while maintaining all standard properties. Central in poset dynamics and crystal base theory.
entries.input: Standard Young tableau T of shape λ
entries.output: Standard Young tableau evac(T) of same shape λ

entries.name: Dual evacuation
entries.description: Variant of evacuation operating on the dual/column structure.

entries.name: Promotion
entries.description: Cyclic operator on standard Young tableaux: removes the entry 1 (via jeu-de-taquin), then relabels all entries by subtracting 1, and places n in the vacated cell. Generates a cyclic action on tableaux of rectangular shape.
entries.input: Standard Young tableau T with entries {1, ..., n}
entries.output: Standard Young tableau pro(T) with entries {1, ..., n}

entries.name: Jeu-de-taquin sliding operator
entries.description: Transforms skew Young tableaux into normal-shape standard tableaux via deterministic inner corner slides. Each slide moves an entry into an adjacent empty cell, maintaining row and column ordering. Confluence: the result is independent of the order of slides.
entries.input: Skew Young tableau of shape λ/μ
entries.output: Standard Young tableau of normal shape
entries.preserved: Knuth equivalence class, recording tableau shape
entries.complexity: O(n) per slide; O(n^2) for full rectification

entries.name: Row insertion (Schensted insertion)
entries.description: Core subroutine of RSK: inserts an element into a semistandard Young tableau by bumping entries along rows. Each insertion increases the tableau by one cell.
entries.input: Semistandard Young tableau T + element x
entries.output: Semistandard Young tableau T' with one additional cell
entries.broken: Shape (grows by one cell), specific entry positions (bumping cascade)
entries.complexity: O(n) per insertion (bumping path is at most n)

entries.name: Reverse-complement operator
entries.description: Applies both reversal (reading entries in reverse order) and complementation (replacing entry i with n+1-i) to a tableau or permutation.
entries.input: Standard Young tableau or permutation on {1,...,n}

entries.name: Kostka transition map
entries.description: Expresses the change-of-basis matrix between Schur functions (s_λ) and monomial symmetric functions (m_μ). The matrix entries are the Kostka numbers K_{λ,μ}, counting semistandard Young tableaux of shape λ and weight μ.
entries.preserved: Symmetric function identity (same element of Λ, different basis)
entries.complexity: O(p(n)^2) where p(n) = number of partitions of n (matrix multiplication)

entries.name: Kronecker product (of symmetric functions)
entries.description: Binary operation on symmetric functions corresponding to the tensor product of representations of the symmetric group. The Kronecker coefficients g_{λ,μ,ν} are notoriously difficult to compute and lack a combinatorial interpretation.
entries.output: Symmetric function s_λ * s_μ = Σ g_{λ,μ,ν} s_ν
entries.complexity: Computationally hard; Kronecker coefficients lack efficient general algorithm

entries.name: Weak equivalence rectangulation mapping
entries.description: Bijection mapping weak equivalence classes of rectangulations (decompositions of a rectangle into smaller rectangles) to specific permutation families.
entries.preserved: Cardinality (bijective), adjacency structure encoded in permutation pattern

entries.name: Strong equivalence rectangulation mapping
entries.description: Bijection mapping strong equivalence classes of rectangulations to permutation families. Stronger equivalence relation than D1-085.

entries.name: Baxter permutation mapping
entries.description: Bijection between Baxter permutations and specific geometric/combinatorial objects (twin binary trees, plane bipolar orientations, rectangulations).
entries.output: Paired combinatorial structure (e.g., pair of binary trees)

entries.name: Twisted Baxter permutation mapping
entries.description: Bijection involving twisted Baxter permutations, a variant of Baxter permutations with modified pattern avoidance conditions.

entries.name: 2-clumped permutation mapping
entries.description: Bijection mapping 2-clumped permutations to specific rectangulation configurations.

entries.name: Co-twisted Baxter permutation mapping
entries.description: Dual bijection to D1-088, mapping co-twisted Baxter permutations to combinatorial structures.

entries.name: Co-2-clumped permutation mapping
entries.description: Dual bijection to D1-089.

entries.name: Weak guillotine rectangulation mapping
entries.description: Bijection involving guillotine rectangulations (those obtainable by recursive straight cuts) under weak equivalence.

entries.name: Strong guillotine rectangulation mapping
entries.description: Bijection involving guillotine rectangulations under strong equivalence.

entries.name: Dyck path bijection
entries.description: Bijection mapping Dyck paths (sequences of up/down steps that never go below the x-axis) to balanced parenthesizations, planar trees, non-crossing partitions, and other Catalan structures. The canonical example of a Catalan bijection.
entries.output: Any of: balanced parenthesization, planar tree with n+1 leaves, triangulation of (n+2)-gon, etc.
entries.preserved: Bijectivity, Catalan number C_n, structural encodings
entries.broken: Specific representation (path vs tree vs parenthesization)

entries.name: Multiset bijection
entries.description: Bijection mapping multisets to lattice paths or other combinatorial objects, encoding the "stars and bars" correspondence.
entries.input: Multiset of size k from alphabet of size n
entries.output: Lattice path or equivalent combinatorial encoding

entries.name: Composition bijection
entries.description: Bijection mapping compositions (ordered partitions) of n to subsets of {1,...,n-1} or binary strings. Encodes the canonical correspondence between compositions and 2^{n-1} subsets.
entries.output: Subset of {1,...,n-1} or binary string of length n-1
entries.preserved: Bijectivity, part structure encoded in subset positions

entries.name: Cartesian product mapping (of posets)
entries.description: Constructs the product poset from two posets: (a,b) <= (a',b') iff a <= a' and b <= b'. The componentwise ordering.
entries.preserved: Partial order axioms, lattice property (if both inputs are lattices)
entries.broken: Totality (product of total orders is generally not total), dimension (increased)

entries.name: Order isomorphism
entries.description: A bijection between posets that preserves the ordering in both directions: f(a) ≤ f(b) iff a ≤ b. The strongest structure-preserving map between posets.
entries.output: Poset (Q, ≤_Q) with explicit bijection f: P -> Q
entries.preserved: Complete order structure, Hasse diagram (up to relabeling)
entries.complexity: Unknown in general (isomorphism testing for posets)

entries.name: Galois connection
entries.description: A pair of order-reversing (antitone) maps f: P -> Q and g: Q -> P with a ≤ g(f(a)) for all a in P and b ≤ f(g(b)) for all b in Q. Both composites g∘f and f∘g are closure operators. Captures dual relationships between posets without a bijection. (The monotone convention instead has f(a) ≤ b iff a ≤ g(b), giving a ≤ g(f(a)) and f(g(b)) ≤ b.)
entries.output: Pair of maps (f, g) forming adjunction
entries.preserved: Closure operators induced on both sides (f∘g and g∘f), fixed point correspondence
entries.broken: Individual element ordering (only closure images are well-behaved)
entries.complexity: Depends on representation; polynomial for finite posets

landed.description: A pair of order-reversing (antitone) maps f: P -> Q, g: Q -> P satisfying: a ≤ g(f(a)) and f(g(b)) ≤ b for all a in P, b in Q. Captures dual relationships between posets even without bijection. Maps directly onto the lattice of flats in matroid theory.

corrected.reason: Graded wrong: the landed text states antitone maps with the monotone convention's second inequality. The claim about matroid flats was not checked and is dropped.

receipts.quote: are the associated closure operators; they are monotone idempotent maps with the property
∀ a b, l a ≤ b ↔ a ≤ u b

lean.note: The corrected definition is equivalent to b ≤ f(a) iff a ≤ g(b).
An antitone Galois connection is exactly a Galois connection in Mathlib's sense into the order dual: an adjunction.
g∘f is a closure operator (Mathlib's ClosureOperator).
f∘g is a closure operator. The fixed-point correspondence is not yet proved.
The landed definition admits (not, const true) on Bool, a Galois connection in neither convention: why the field was corrected.

formal.note: Mathlib's Galois connection is the monotone convention: l a <= b iff a <= u b, giving a <= u(l a) and l(u b) <= b. The entry states antitone maps but gives the monotone pair of inequalities. For antitone maps the second must read b <= f(g(b)); with that correction both composites are closure operators, as the entry's preserved field says (in Mathlib, an antitone connection is a monotone one into the order dual).
The unit inequality a <= g(f(a)), which holds in both conventions.
In the monotone convention only u after l is a closure operator (l after u is an interior operator). The entry's claim that both composites are closure operators is the antitone case.

entries.name: Closure operator
entries.description: Unary transformation on a poset mapping each element to its minimum bounding element. Must satisfy three axioms: extensive (x ≤ cl(x)), monotone (x ≤ y implies cl(x) ≤ cl(y)), and idempotent (cl(cl(x)) = cl(x)). Maps onto the lattice of flats in matroid theory, bridging algebra and geometric independence.
entries.preserved: Partial order, lattice of closed elements forms a complete lattice
entries.broken: Distinctness of elements (many elements may close to the same value)
entries.complexity: Depends on representation; O(n) per element for matroid closure

entries.name: Order embedding
entries.description: An injective map f: P -> Q satisfying f(a) ≤ f(b) iff a ≤ b. Preserves and reflects the order but need not be surjective. Embeds one poset into another as a sub-poset.
entries.preserved: Complete order structure of P within Q
entries.broken: Surjectivity (Q may be larger), completeness properties of P
entries.complexity: Depends on target poset; polynomial for explicit constructions

entries.name: Supremum preservation mapping
entries.description: An order-preserving map f: P -> Q that additionally preserves all existing suprema (least upper bounds): f(sup(S)) = sup(f(S)) for all S ⊆ P where sup(S) exists.
entries.output: Lattice/poset (Q, ≤) with suprema preserved by image

entries.name: Infimum preservation mapping
entries.description: Dual of D1-102: preserves all existing infima (greatest lower bounds).
entries.output: Lattice/poset with infima preserved by image

entries.name: Thue-Morse morphism
entries.description: Word morphism μ: a -> ab, b -> ba. Iterated application produces the Thue-Morse sequence, which is overlap-free (contains no factor of the form axaxa). Proves existence of infinite repetition-free sequences over a binary alphabet.
entries.input: Character in {a, b} (or word over {a, b} via morphism extension)
entries.output: Word over {a, b} (doubled length per application)
entries.preserved: Alphabet {a, b}, overlap-freeness of fixed point
entries.broken: Word length (doubled each iteration), specific character positions
entries.complexity: O(2^n) to generate n iterations (output doubles each step)

entries.name: Fibonacci morphism
entries.description: Word morphism φ: a -> ab, b -> a. Iterated application produces the infinite Fibonacci word, whose character frequencies converge to the golden ratio. A Sturmian sequence.
entries.input: Character in {a, b} (or word via morphism extension)
entries.complexity: O(F_n) to generate n iterations (Fibonacci growth)

entries.name: Erasing morphism
entries.description: A word morphism that maps at least one character to the empty string. Used for projection, subsequence extraction, and isolating periodic points of iterated morphisms.
entries.output: Word over alphabet Σ' ⊆ Σ (characters in kernel are deleted)
entries.broken: Word length (reduced), characters in the kernel

entries.name: Iterated morphism mapping
entries.description: General framework: apply a word morphism repeatedly to generate a sequence of words converging to a fixed point (when it exists). The Thue-Morse and Fibonacci morphisms are specific instances.
entries.input: Word morphism σ: Σ* -> Σ* + seed word w
entries.output: Sequence of words σ^n(w), potentially converging to a fixed point
entries.preserved: Morphism structure, recurrence relations in the generated sequence

entries.name: Rigid transformation (isometry)
entries.description: Distance-preserving map of Euclidean space. Umbrella term for translations, reflections, rotations, and glide reflections. In Domain 1 context: applied to finite geometric configurations for design theory.
entries.preserved: All distances, all angles, size, shape

entries.name: Translation
entries.description: Slides every point by the same displacement vector.
entries.preserved: All distances, angles, size, shape, orientation

entries.name: Reflection
entries.description: Maps each point to its mirror image across a hyperplane (line in 2D, plane in 3D).

entries.name: Rotation
entries.description: Maps each point by rotating about a center point (2D) or axis (3D) by a specified angle.
entries.preserved: All distances, angles, size, shape, orientation
entries.broken: Position of non-center points, specific coordinates
entries.complexity: O(d^2) per point (matrix multiplication) or O(d) for 2D

entries.name: Non-rigid transformation
entries.description: Umbrella term for transformations that alter size while preserving shape (dilations) or alter angles (shearing).
entries.preserved: Depends on specific type (dilation preserves shape, shearing preserves area)

entries.name: Dilation (scaling)
entries.description: Scales a figure by a factor k from a center point. Preserves shape and angles but changes size. In Domain 1 context: maps affine/projective planes into different scalar configurations for design construction.
entries.input: Geometric figure + center + scale factor k
entries.broken: Absolute distances (multiplied by k), absolute size

entries.name: Affine transformation
entries.description: Composition of a linear map and a translation. Preserves collinearity and ratios of distances along lines but not absolute distances or angles.
entries.preserved: Collinearity, parallelism, distance ratios along lines, convexity

entries.name: Projective transformation
entries.description: Maps projective space to itself preserving collinearity (maps lines to lines). More general than affine. Central in finite projective geometry for design construction.
entries.broken: Parallelism (not a projective concept), absolute distances

entries.name: Block design construction
entries.description: Transforms a base set of v elements into a family of k-element subsets (blocks) satisfying prescribed intersection and balance conditions. General framework encompassing BIBDs, resolvable designs, and group divisible designs.
entries.input: Element set of size v + parameters (k, λ, r, b)
entries.output: Collection of blocks satisfying design axioms
entries.preserved: Balance conditions (each element in r blocks, each pair in λ blocks)
entries.complexity: Varies widely; existence is often the hard problem

entries.name: Pairwise balanced uniform design (PBD) construction
entries.description: Constructs a design where every pair of elements occurs in exactly λ blocks, but block sizes may vary. Generalization of BIBD where uniform block size is relaxed.
entries.input: Element set of size v + pair-balance parameter λ
entries.output: Collection of blocks (varying sizes) with pairwise balance
entries.complexity: Varies; recursive constructions are polynomial given base designs

entries.name: Steiner triple system construction
entries.description: Constructs a design where every pair of elements occurs in exactly one block of size 3. Exists iff v ≡ 1 or 3 (mod 6). A specific BIBD with k=3, λ=1.
entries.input: Element set of size v where v ≡ 1 or 3 (mod 6)
entries.output: Collection of 3-element blocks covering all pairs exactly once
entries.preserved: Triple coverage of all pairs, block size = 3
entries.broken: Element freedom (fully constrained by triple system)
entries.complexity: Polynomial for known constructions (e.g., Bose, Skolem)

entries.name: Symmetric BIBD construction
entries.description: Constructs a balanced incomplete block design where the number of blocks equals the number of elements (b = v). Equivalently, each pair of blocks intersects in exactly λ elements (duality between elements and blocks).
entries.input: Parameters (v, k, λ) satisfying b = v
entries.broken: Asymmetry between elements and blocks (they are now symmetric)
entries.complexity: Varies; existence constrained by necessary conditions on (v,k,lambda)

entries.name: Incidence matrix transformation
entries.description: Maps a combinatorial design (or graph, or hypergraph) to its incidence matrix: rows = elements (or vertices), columns = blocks (or edges), entry = 1 iff element is in block. Translates combinatorial structure into linear algebra.
entries.preserved: Incidence structure (element-block containment), balance parameters encoded in row/column sums
entries.complexity: O(|V| * |E|) or O(v * b) for designs

entries.name: Translation
entries.description: Slides figure along displacement vector.

entries.name: Reflection
entries.description: Mirror image across axis/hyperplane.

entries.name: Rotation
entries.description: Turns figure around center/axis by angle.

entries.name: Dilation (Scaling)
entries.description: Scales by factor k from center. Affine, not isometric.

entries.name: Vertical Shift
entries.description: g(x) = f(x) + c. Shifts graph vertically.

entries.name: Horizontal Shift
entries.description: g(x) = f(x+c). Positive c shifts left.

entries.name: Vertical Scaling
entries.description: g(x) = a*f(x).

entries.name: Horizontal Scaling
entries.description: g(x) = f(a*x). a>1 compresses.

entries.name: Affine Transformation
entries.description: Linear map + translation. Preserves collinearity.

entries.name: Collineation
entries.description: Bijective map of projective space preserving collinearity. All collineations are semilinear.

entries.name: Involution (algebraic)
entries.description: Self-inverse map: f(f(x)) = x.

entries.name: Fourier Transform
entries.description: Decomposes function into frequency components via complex exponential kernel.
entries.input: Function f in L^1(R) or L^2(R)
entries.output: Fourier transform f-hat in frequency domain

entries.name: Fourier Cosine Transform
entries.description: Real-valued variant using cosine kernel for even functions.

entries.name: Fourier Sine Transform
entries.description: Real-valued variant using sine kernel for odd functions.

entries.name: Fractional Fourier Transform
entries.description: Continuous interpolation between function and Fourier transform, parameterized by angle.

entries.name: Short-time Fourier Transform
entries.description: Fourier transform through sliding window for time-frequency localization.
entries.broken: Global frequency resolution (traded for time localization)

entries.name: Rectangular Mask STFT
entries.description: Short-time Fourier transform with a rectangular (boxcar) window: the Fourier transform of each windowed segment.
entries.preserved: Energy up to window normalization; invertibility with sufficient overlap
entries.broken: Frequency resolution (sidelobe leakage from the sharp window)

entries.name: Fourier-Bros-Iagolnitzer Transform
entries.description: FBI transform for microlocal analysis with Gaussian window.

entries.name: Gabor Transform
entries.description: STFT with Gaussian window, optimal time-frequency localization.

entries.name: Hankel Transform
entries.description: Bessel function kernel for cylindrically symmetric functions.

entries.name: Hartley Transform
entries.description: Real-valued Fourier alternative using cas(x) = cos(x)+sin(x).

entries.name: Hermite Transform
entries.description: Expansion in Hermite function basis.
entries.preserved: Orthogonality in Gaussian-weighted space, quantum oscillator eigenstates

entries.name: Hilbert Transform
entries.description: Principal value integral relating real/imaginary parts of analytic signal.
entries.output: Hilbert transform Hf (imaginary part of analytic signal)
entries.preserved: L^2 norm, analytic signal construction, power spectrum

entries.name: Jacobi Transform
entries.description: Integral transform with Jacobi polynomial kernel.

entries.name: Laguerre Transform
entries.description: Expansion in Laguerre function basis.

entries.name: Laplace Transform
entries.description: Maps to complex frequency domain via exponential kernel e^{-st}.
entries.input: Function f(t) on [0,inf) with exponential growth bound

entries.name: Inverse Laplace Transform
entries.description: Recovers time-domain function via Bromwich integral.

entries.name: Two-sided Laplace Transform
entries.description: The bilateral Laplace transform F(s) = integral over R of f(t) e^{-s t} dt, converging in a vertical strip; contains the Fourier transform on the imaginary axis and the moment generating function.
entries.output: Analytic function F(s) on a strip
entries.preserved: Convolution to product; information (invertible within the strip)
entries.broken: Causality information unless the strip is specified

entries.name: Inverse Two-sided Laplace Transform
entries.description: Recovers f from its bilateral Laplace transform by a Bromwich integral along a vertical line inside the strip of convergence.
entries.input: Analytic F(s) and its strip of convergence
entries.broken: Nothing, given the strip; without it the inverse is ambiguous

entries.name: Linear Canonical Transform
entries.description: Four-parameter family generalizing Fourier, Laplace, fractional Fourier.

entries.name: Mellin Transform
entries.description: Multiplicative Laplace analogue. Kernel t^{s-1}.
entries.output: M{f}(s) in vertical strip of convergence

formal.note: The integral of t^(s-1) f(t) over (0, infinity): the entry's kernel.

Mathlib gives the exact law: dilating f by a multiplies the transform by a^(-s). "Scale invariance" holds only for the modulus on the line Re s = 0. The convolution-to-product rule the entry also claims is not in Mathlib at the pin.

entries.name: Inverse Mellin Transform
entries.description: Inversion of Mellin transform.

entries.name: Poisson-Mellin-Newton Cycle
entries.description: The triangle of correspondences between Poisson generating functions, Mellin transforms and Newton (finite difference) series used in the analysis of algorithms (Flajolet and coauthors): a sequence's asymptotics read from the poles of a Mellin transform via Rice's integrals.
entries.reading: Recorded from memory of the analytic-combinatorics literature.

entries.name: Radon Transform
entries.description: Integrates function over hyperplanes. Core of tomographic reconstruction.
entries.preserved: Injectivity (for suitable classes), inversion formula, slice theorem

entries.name: Penrose Transform
entries.description: Maps twistor space cohomology to spacetime field equation solutions.
entries.input: Cohomology class on projective twistor space
entries.output: Solution of zero-rest-mass field equation on M^4

entries.name: Harish-Chandra Transform
entries.description: The spherical transform on a reductive group: integrates a K-bi-invariant function against spherical functions, reducing harmonic analysis on G/K to Fourier analysis on a Cartan subspace modulo the Weyl group.
entries.preserved: Convolution to product; Plancherel (with Harish-Chandra's c-function)

entries.name: Fourier-Stieltjes Transform
entries.description: The Fourier transform of a finite measure: mu-hat(xi) = integral e^{-i x xi} d mu(x). Characteristic functions of probability measures are the case of positive mass one.
entries.preserved: Convolution to product; measure determined (uniqueness); positive definiteness (Bochner)
entries.broken: Decay (mu-hat need not vanish at infinity)

entries.name: Z-transform
entries.description: Transforms a sequence x_n to X(z) = sum x_n z^{-n}, converging in an annulus; the discrete analogue of the Laplace transform.
entries.preserved: Convolution to product; information within the region of convergence
entries.broken: Causality information unless the region is specified

entries.name: Fourier-Mukai Transform
entries.description: Integral functor on derived categories of coherent sheaves. Uses kernel on product variety X x Y. Defines derived equivalence. NOT a clone of classical Fourier.
entries.input: Object in D^b(Coh(X)) + kernel P on X x Y
entries.complexity: Depends on kernel; derived category operations

entries.name: LU Decomposition
entries.description: Factors A = LU (lower x upper triangular). Matrix Gaussian elimination.

entries.name: LDU Decomposition
entries.description: Variant extracting diagonal: A = LDU.

entries.name: LUP Decomposition
entries.description: LU with permutation for pivoting. PA = LU. Exists for all square matrices.

entries.name: Block LU Decomposition
entries.description: LU on block-partitioned matrices. Optimized for parallel architectures.
entries.preserved: Same as LU at block level

entries.name: Rank Factorization
entries.description: A = CF where C is m x r full column rank, F is r x n full row rank.
entries.output: C (m x r) * F (r x n)

entries.name: Cholesky Decomposition
entries.description: A = U*U for Hermitian positive-definite. Half cost of LU.

entries.name: LDL Decomposition
entries.description: Cholesky variant without square roots: A = LDL*.
entries.preserved: Same as Cholesky, no square roots

entries.name: QR Decomposition
entries.description: A = QR with Q orthogonal, R upper triangular. Numerically stable least squares.

entries.name: Eigendecomposition (Spectral Decomposition)
entries.description: A = VDV^{-1}. Diagonalizes matrix. Enables A^n = VD^nV^{-1}.

entries.name: Spectral Decomposition
entries.description: A = VDV^{-1}. Diagonalizes matrix. Enables A^n = VD^nV^{-1}.

entries.name: Jordan Normal Form
entries.description: Block-diagonal form for non-diagonalizable matrices. Jordan blocks with eigenvalue on diagonal, 1's on superdiagonal.
entries.input: Square matrix over algebraically closed field

entries.name: Jordan-Chevalley Decomposition
entries.description: A = D + N (commuting diag + nilpotent).
entries.input: Linear operator on fin-dim space over perfect field
entries.preserved: Eigenvalues in D, nilpotent index in N

entries.name: Schur Decomposition
entries.description: A = UTU* with U unitary, T upper triangular. Eigenvalues on diagonal of T. Numerically stable.

entries.name: Real Schur Decomposition
entries.description: Real arithmetic Schur: T quasi-upper-triangular with 2x2 blocks for complex eigenvalue pairs.
entries.preserved: Real eigenvalues on diagonal, complex pairs in 2x2 blocks

entries.name: QZ Decomposition (Generalized Schur)
entries.description: Simultaneous reduction of (A,B) for generalized eigenvalue problem Ax = λBx.

entries.name: Hessenberg Decomposition

entries.description: A = UTV* with T triangular, U,V unitary. Robust SVD generalization.

entries.name: Polar Decomposition

entries.name: Algebraic Polar Decomposition

entries.name: Mostow's Decomposition
entries.description: A = U * e^{iM} * e^S (U unitary, M antisymmetric, S symmetric).

entries.name: Sectoral Decomposition
entries.description: Decomposes matrix by angular eigenvalue properties.

entries.name: Matrix Square Root

entries.name: Smith Normal Form
entries.description: Reduces PID matrix to diagonal via unimodular ops. Invariant factors with d_i | d_{i+1}. Proves Fundamental Theorem of Finitely Generated Abelian Groups.

entries.name: Hermite Normal Form
entries.description: Integer row echelon form via unimodular row ops. Unique canonical lattice basis.

entries.name: Rational Canonical Form (Frobenius Normal Form)
entries.description: Block diagonal of companion matrices for invariant factors. Works over any field.

entries.name: Frobenius Normal Form
entries.description: Block diagonal of companion matrices for invariant factors. Works over any field.

entries.name: Gram-Schmidt Orthogonalization
entries.description: Transforms linearly independent vectors to orthonormal set spanning same subspace.

entries.name: Localization

entries.name: Completion (I-adic)

entries.name: Quotient Ring Construction
entries.description: R/I: elements of I become zero. Geometrically restricts to subvariety.

entries.name: Field of Fractions Construction
entries.description: Integral domain to smallest containing field.

entries.name: Product of Rings
